headline: SPD officer fired for sharing Flock login with ICE agent husband, who ran 983 unauthorized searches
summary: Former Savannah police officer Amber Harpe was terminated after an investigation revealed she shared her Flock login with her ICE agent husband, who then performed nearly 1,000 unauthorized license plate searches.
details: Former Savannah police officer Amber Harpe was fired in August after an investigation found she shared her Flock login with her husband, Tyler Harpe, an ICE agent. The Savannah Police Department (SPD) does not share its Flock data with ICE, and sharing access violated department security protocols.

While he had unauthorized access, Tyler Harpe conducted 983 searches related to 97 license plates. A local ABC affiliate, WJCL, reported that these searches overwhelmingly targeted vehicles registered to Hispanic drivers. The Harpes maintained that their actions were for "law-enforcement purposes" and not personal.

Initially, an eight-hour suspension was recommended for Harpe. However, Major Michelle Halford and Assistant Police Chief Robert Gavin overruled this, leading to her removal from the force. Harpe was one of six SPD employees fired following an internal investigation into Flock misuse, though she was not among the four later arrested.

headline_marked: [[Google renames Gemini features]] again, migrating Gems to Skills starting November 17
headline: Google renames Gemini features again, migrating Gems to Skills starting November 17
summary: Starting November 17, personal Gems will be force-migrated to Skills, while Spark is being rebranded as 'Task'. Learn what each feature does and how to prepare for the changes.
details: Google is once again reorganizing and renaming its AI features, a move that will impact personal accounts starting November 17. The company will begin force-migrating existing 'Gems' into a new format called 'Skills', with work and school accounts to follow in 2027.

Previously, Gems were standalone custom bots accessed from a sidebar. Skills integrate custom instructions directly into the main chat, activated by typing a forward slash. Gemini can also apply a Skill automatically when relevant to a prompt.

A significant upgrade is the ability to 'stack' multiple Skills in one conversation, allowing for complex instructions like enforcing branding and setting writing tone simultaneously. However, many built-in Gem tools like Canvas, Deep Research, Guided Learning, and media generation are not yet compatible with Skills.

Additionally, Skills currently lack sharing capabilities and direct file attachments from Google Drive, though Google states these features are coming soon. Users with Gems relying on these functions should test them before the November 17 migration.

Another feature, Scheduled Actions, allows users to set prompts for Gemini to run at specified intervals, preparing results in the background. Up to 10 actions can run concurrently, and a Google AI subscription is no longer required, though it needs Keep Activity enabled.

Scheduled Actions prepare results an hour before delivery, making them suitable for non-time-sensitive information like daily calendar digests or weather forecasts. A key limitation is that location-dependent actions use the setup location and do not update if the user travels.

For event-reactive tasks, Google's background agent 'Spark' is being rebranded as 'Task'. This always-on agent runs on Google Cloud virtual machines, continuing its work even after devices are closed or locked.

Users give Spark/Task high-level goals, and it works through steps independently. Google has built in safeguards, prompting for user approval before sending messages, changing data, making purchases, or submitting web forms. It also hands control back for passwords or payment details.

While these safeguards are in place, Google advises users to monitor important tasks. Users can run up to 15 tasks simultaneously, though a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription is required for this feature.
